Heart failure code sets (all versions)

Source: R/conditions.R
hf_codes.Rd

get_hf_vN_codes() returns the ICD code set for version N of the heart failure definition, and get_hf_vN_defs() displays its narrative algorithm. Heart failure is both a condition (history) and an outcome definition: the condition definition counts inpatient or repeated outpatient claims in any diagnosis position, while the outcome definition requires an overnight hospitalization with a primary discharge diagnosis of heart failure. Each version is frozen once released: later versions never change what an earlier version's functions return.

Usage

get_hf_v1_codes(
  code_type = NULL,
  variable_type = c("condition", "outcome"),
  periods = FALSE,
  priority = 1L
)

get_hf_v1_defs(variable_type = c("condition", "outcome"))

get_hf_v2_codes(
  code_type = NULL,
  variable_type = c("condition", "outcome"),
  periods = FALSE,
  priority = 1L
)

get_hf_v2_defs(variable_type = c("condition", "outcome"))

Arguments

code_type

Optional character vector of code types to return. Valid values: "dx_icd9", "dx_icd10", "proc_icd9", "proc_icd10", "hcpcs", "cpt", "rev". NULL (default) returns all code types.

variable_type

"condition" (default) or "outcome". Both are defined for heart failure; in v2 the outcome set also includes I11.0, I13.0 and I13.2.

periods

Logical. FALSE (default) returns short-format codes (e.g., "4010"). TRUE returns decimal-format codes (e.g., "401.0").

priority

Integer vector subsetting confidence tiers to include (1 = core, 2 = probable, 3 = cautious). Default 1.

Value

get_hf_vN_codes(): a tibble with columns type, code, priority, version, and definition (plus acuity, required_secondary and qualifies_as_primary for v2 outcomes). get_hf_vN_defs(): the narrative definition (displayed, and returned invisibly), or NULL.

Versions

v1

ICD-9 402.01, 402.11, 402.91, 404.01, 404.03, 404.11, 404.13, 404.91, 404.93, 428.x; and ICD-10 I11.0, I13.0, I13.2, I50.x.

v2

ICD-10 only, so claims before October 1, 2015 cannot qualify. History uses every billable I50 code; I11.0, I13.0 and I13.2 are left out because they require a secondary I50.x on the same claim. Outcomes use all of those codes plus per-code columns that describe the rules (see below).

v2 outcome code attributes

get_hf_v2_codes(variable_type = "outcome") has three extra columns, which illustrate the outcome rules and are not applied by the package:

acuity

"acute", "acute_on_chronic", "chronic" or "unspecified" for I50 codes (including I50.814, I50.82, I50.83 and I50.84, whose descriptors give no acuity); NA for I11.0, I13.0 and I13.2.

required_secondary

Codes that must appear in non-primary positions: "I50.x" for I11.0, "I50.x + N18.x" for I13.0 and I13.2, otherwise "none".

qualifies_as_primary

TRUE for the acute and acute-on-chronic I50 codes and for I11.0, I13.0 and I13.2 (subject to required_secondary). Chronic and unspecified I50 codes can be the secondary code, or count toward incident heart failure, but do not qualify as the primary diagnosis of an acute heart failure hospitalization.

Version history

Every version below remains available. Compare any of them with get_version_diffs("hf"); list them with list_versions("hf").

  • v1: initial version (54 codes).

  • v2 (2026-10-23, 23 codes): ICD-10 only; history uses I50.x; outcomes add I11.0, I13.0, I13.2 with acuity rules.

    • Why: Restricts heart failure to ICD-10-CM codes. Drops all ICD-9 codes (402.x1, 404.x1, 404.x3 and 428.x), so claims and hospitalizations before October 1, 2015 cannot qualify. History no longer uses I11.0, I13.0 and I13.2, which require a secondary I50.x on the same claim, so it is I50.x only. The outcome definition is rebuilt around acute heart failure hospitalization (an acute or acute-on-chronic I50 code as the primary diagnosis, or I11.0, I13.0 or I13.2 as the primary diagnosis with the required secondary codes) and incident heart failure (any I50 code). The outcome code set carries acuity, required_secondary and qualifies_as_primary columns that describe these rules.

    • Condition codes compared with v1:

      • Removed 31 codes:

        • dx_icd9 (28): 40201, 40211, 40291, 40401, 40403, 40411, 40413, 40491, 40493, 428, 4280, 4281, 4282, 42820, 42821, 42822, 42823, 4283, 42830, 42831, 42832, 42833, 4284, 42840, 42841, 42842, 42843, 4289

        • dx_icd10 (3): I110, I130, I132

    • Outcome codes compared with v1:

      • Removed 28 codes:

        • dx_icd9 (28): 40201, 40211, 40291, 40401, 40403, 40411, 40413, 40491, 40493, 428, 4280, 4281, 4282, 42820, 42821, 42822, 42823, 4283, 42830, 42831, 42832, 42833, 4284, 42840, 42841, 42842, 42843, 4289

See also

get_version_diffs(), list_versions(), spec_hf_v1, spec_hf_v2

#> ℹ Acute heart failure hospitalization: an overnight hospitalization with
#>   either:
#> • a primary discharge diagnosis of an acute or acute-on-chronic I50 code
#>   (I50.21, I50.23, I50.31, I50.33, I50.41, I50.43, I50.811, I50.813); or
#> • a primary diagnosis of I11.0 with any I50 code in a non-primary position; or
#>   a primary diagnosis of I13.0 or I13.2 with both any I50 code and any N18 code
#>   in non-primary positions.
#> ! I50 codes with chronic or unspecified acuity (e.g., I50.9, I50.22) do not
#>   qualify as the primary diagnosis, but any I50 code can be the secondary code
#>   in the I11.0/I13.x rule. I50.84 (end-stage) does not qualify as a primary
#>   diagnosis.
#> ℹ Incident heart failure:
#> • any I50 code in any position during follow-up, with no I50, I11.0, I13.0 or
#>   I13.2 in the baseline period. Baseline and follow-up windows are defined by
#>   the study.
#> ! ICD-10 only: hospitalizations before October 1, 2015 (ICD-9 era) cannot
#>   qualify. Position rules are applied outside the package; see the acuity,
#>   required_secondary and qualifies_as_primary columns of the outcome code set.
